api.note: API v1 alone does not establish review-v2 or private Web auth-status capability.

features.note: All three features are additive on review-v2 only. dense-128 raises the finding page from 32 to 128 and stays bounded by the 64 KiB body ceiling Core 0.10.0 serves, and reason-v1 adds a reason to each not_evaluated finding. A request without the header answers the published 32-finding, seven-key document; a header on review-v1, an unknown or repeated token, or an empty part is invalid_request, and a response that enabled a feature echoes the accepted set in the same header. ambiguous-mention-v1 (Core 0.14.0) requires reason-v1 and reports a one-character resonator name the matcher could not settle, whose source text meets the evidence threshold, as a not_evaluated finding with reason ambiguous_mention. clients_request is the pair Web 0.5.0 and later and Windows 0.7.0 and later send on every review-v2 request; they add ambiguous-mention-v1 only when GET /v1/capabilities lists it.

manuscript.note: v1 and v2 keep their meaning, and an imported v1 or v2 report, a document-mode choice or a semantic decision stays history, not a fresh check. v3 adds per-segment term results for long manuscripts: a saved segment result is reused only when its content hashes, review basis and request inputs all match a live review-v2 basis. v4 keeps v3's 13 top-level keys, the 44 MiB file limit and the canonical bytes, and raises the findings, resolutions and choices limits from 32 to 128 while allowing a reason on a not_evaluated finding; only the label v4 brings those limits, so a v1, v2 or v3 file keeps its 32-item caps and rejects reason. A writer stores the lowest format that holds the content (v1/v2, then v3, then v4, then v5). v5 adds a review_features list, the ambiguous_mention reason and segmentation-v1-gaps segment records and otherwise keeps v4; it ships in Web 0.5.0 through 0.8.0 and Windows 0.7.0 through 0.10.0, and Web 0.4.5 and earlier and Windows 0.6.6 and earlier reject a v5 file. The v4 contract ships in Web 0.4.0, 0.4.1 and 0.4.2 and in Windows 0.6.0, 0.6.1 and 0.6.2, not in Web 0.3.1 or Windows 0.5.1, which reject a v4 file; the shipped-release records below keep the format each release was recorded with.

compatibility.note: The client reads wuwaterm-manuscript-v1 through v5 and writes the lowest format that holds the content: v5 only for a recorded review feature or gap-tolerant segment records. Windows 0.6.6 and earlier reject v5 files. The structure check and the single-character list need a service that lists structure-check-v1 and ambiguous-mention-v1; reading the served dictionary identity directly needs dictionary-identity-v1. Local manuscript editing works offline, and online features require a configured API and device credential.

compatibility.note: The Web BFF validates response shapes strictly; a matching API version alone does not prove compatibility. The client writes wuwaterm-manuscript-v5 only for a recorded review feature or gap-tolerant segment records and keeps the lowest earlier format otherwise; Web 0.4.5 and earlier and Windows 0.6.6 and earlier reject v5 files. The structure check and ambiguous single characters appear only when the Core API lists structure-check-v1 and ambiguous-mention-v1.
